stories.title: Masked settlers attack olive harvest in West Bank, injuring Palestinians and journalist
stories.summary: Dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives near the village of Abu Falah in the occupied West Bank, setting fire to cars and olive trees. The violence injured 12 Palestinians, including four who hold dual Palestinian‑American citizenship, and also wounded a foreign journalist. One of the injured, Majdi, an American citizen, suffered deep head wounds from nail‑studded sticks, and his elderly mother was also hurt.
stories.why: The incident underscores escalating settler violence that endangers civilians and press freedom in the occupied territories.
stories.change: New high-signal event entered the brief.

stories.title: Twelve ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz during week of Oct 5‑11, highest since war began
stories.summary: BBC Verify analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data shows that twelve vessels reported attacks in the Strait of Hormuz between 5 October and 11 October, the highest weekly total since the US‑Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week recorded ten attacks, including six vessels struck on Sunday, with four additional incidents reported later in the week. Industry data indicates the rise in attacks has slowed the recent recovery of oil shipments through the strait.
stories.why: The increase may hinder the recovery of oil shipments through the strait, affecting global energy flows.

stories.title: India’s forex reserves drop $60 billion in six weeks as RBI intervenes
stories.summary: India’s foreign‑exchange reserves fell by roughly $60 billion over a six‑week period. The Reserve Bank of India stepped into the market to support the rupee, which has been among the weakest Asian currencies this year. The drawdown reflects the central bank’s effort to stabilise the currency.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
stories.summary: Five people have been killed and 16 injured in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.
